name: Celtuce
grown_as: Stem lettuce, grown for its thick, crisp stem, which is peeled and eaten; the young leaves are eaten too. William's records give no named variety ('stem lettuce').
habit: A single upright, thick, unbranched stem 30 to 60 cm tall and 3 to 5 cm thick, pale green, set with leaves all the way up and crowned with a loose tuft of leaves at the top, like a small palm. Bolts to 1 m or more and branches at the top to flower.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate, spiralling up the thick stem, crowded into a tuft at the top; the lower ones are stripped or fall as the stem grows
leaf.outline: Long and narrow, lance-shaped, 15 to 30 cm long and 4 to 8 cm wide
leaf.base: Broad and stalkless, joined straight onto the stem
leaf.margin: Smooth or very finely toothed, gently wavy
leaf.veins: A pale midrib running the length of the leaf; side veins slanting forward, faint
leaf.surface: Smooth, hairless and a little shiny, slightly crinkled near the midrib
leaf.colour: Light to mid green, sometimes flushed red at the top of the plant

flower.form: A small head like a little dandelion, made only of strap-shaped florets, opening flat in the morning and closing by midday
flower.petals: No true petals to count: about 10 to 25 strap-shaped florets, each a single ray with five tiny teeth across its squared-off tip, laid out like the rays of a dandelion
flower.centre: No separate eye: the inner florets are shorter and the forked yellow styles stand up in the middle
flower.behind: A slim cylindrical cup (involucre) of narrow green bracts overlapping like roof tiles, longer than wide, sometimes tinged purple
flower.carried: Many heads on short stalks in a wide, branched, flat-topped spray at the top of a tall bolted stem, the heads facing up
flower.season: July to September, after the plant bolts

fruit: Each floret makes one seed (achene): slim, flattened, 3 to 4 mm, with fine lengthwise ribs, narrowing at the top into a thin beak carrying a tuft of soft white hairs (pappus). Seed colour is white-cream, grey, brown or black depending on variety. The heads open into small white fluffy clocks, much smaller and looser than a dandelion clock. The plant has milky sap.
seedling: Two smooth oval seed leaves, then narrow, pointed true leaves, longer than a lettuce's.

leaf: a pale midrib the full length, smooth wavy edge
bloom: a small pale yellow head of strap-shaped florets, like a little dandelion
a slim cup of overlapping green bracts behind
seed: slim, flat, ribbed seed 3 to 4 mm, narrowing to a point
seedling: the first true leaf narrow and pointed
young: an upright rosette of long, narrow, pointed leaves
the stem just starting to lift it off the soil
crop: a thick, pale green, upright stem 30 to 60 cm
long pointed leaves up the stem and a tuft at the top
leaf scars on the lower stem where leaves are gone
flower: the thick stem grown taller, branching at the top
small pale yellow heads in a spray
seedhead: small white fluffy clocks at the branch tips
the tall dried stem, branched at the top

look_alikes: Ordinary lettuce that has bolted has a thinner stem and broader, rounder leaves. Kohlrabi and other stem crops are brassicas with waxy grey leaves.
